title: Taxation of investments in India
quality: Rates cross-checked against reporting of Budget 2026 and the Income-tax framework in force from 1 April 2026. Verify against the Income Tax Department before relying on any figure.
disclaimer: Educational content, not tax advice. Tax outcomes depend on total income, residential status, regime chosen, surcharge, cess, deductions and individual circumstances. Consult a qualified professional for your own position.
notice: The Income Tax Act, 2025 is in force from 1 April 2026. Rates and holding periods are unchanged, but section numbering and the term 'tax year' replace older references. Both the familiar section numbers and the new framework are noted where relevant.

sections.title: How the income is classified
sections.intro: Everything in Indian investment taxation follows from one question: is this a capital gain, or is it business income? The answer decides the rate, the loss rules and the return form.

head: Activity
Head of income
Rate basis
rows: Special rates, subject to fund classification

sections.note: Exchange-traded derivatives in securities satisfying the statutory conditions are non-speculative business, not capital gains. Intraday equity, by contrast, is speculative business. The two are taxed at the same slab rates but their loss rules differ sharply.

sections.title: Capital gains on listed equity
sections.intro: For listed equity and equity-oriented mutual funds where STT has been paid, two rates apply and one holding period separates them.

head: Type
Holding period
Rate
Threshold
rows: First ₹1,25,000 of gains each year exempt

points: The short-term rate rose from 15% to 20%, and the long-term rate from 10% to 12.5%, for transfers on or after 23 July 2024. Budget 2026 made no further change for FY 2026-27.
Indexation was removed for most assets. For land or a building acquired before 23 July 2024, a resident individual or HUF may choose the lower of 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation.
Capital gains taxed at these special rates do not qualify for the section 87A rebate, even where total income is otherwise within the rebate limit.
The regime chosen, old or new, does not change the rate on these special-rate capital gains. It changes how the rest of the income is taxed.

sections.title: Securities Transaction Tax from 1 April 2026
sections.intro: Budget 2026 raised STT on derivatives sharply while leaving cash market rates untouched. The stated intent was to make speculative activity more expensive.
points: For options, STT applies to the premium, not to the notional strike value. This distinction changes the figure by orders of magnitude.
Where trading is assessed as business income, STT paid is generally allowable as a business expense. Where the income is a capital gain, it is not deductible in computing the gain.
STT is rounded to the nearest rupee.

sections.title: Intraday and F&O as business income
sections.intro: Both are business income taxed at slab rates, but they are different kinds of business, and the difference matters most when there is a loss.
sections.note: Carry forward of any of these losses generally requires the return to be filed by the due date. A late return can forfeit the benefit entirely, which is one of the most expensive avoidable mistakes in trading.

sections.title: What F&O turnover actually means
sections.intro: Turnover for income-tax purposes is not the notional value of contracts traded. Confusing the two is the single most common error, and it can wrongly trigger audit thresholds.
points: For futures, turnover is generally taken as the absolute total of favourable and unfavourable differences, that is, the sum of profits and losses treated as positive numbers.
For options, the absolute differences are counted, and in the commonly followed approach premium received on sale is also included, subject to professional judgement and current guidance.
The gross contract value shown on a broker statement is not turnover for this purpose.

example.setup: A trader has one futures trade with a loss of ₹20,000 and another with a profit of ₹35,000.
steps: Net result = 35,000 − 20,000 = ₹15,000 profit, which is the taxable income
The notional contract value across both trades might be several crore, and is not the relevant figure

sections.title: Mutual funds and SIPs
sections.intro: A SIP is not a tax category. Each instalment is a separate purchase with its own date, cost and holding period.
points: Equity-oriented funds follow the equity rates: 20% short-term, 12.5% long-term above the ₹1.25 lakh annual threshold, with 12 months separating the two.
Units are generally treated as redeemed on a first in, first out basis, so the oldest instalments are considered sold first.
A single redemption can therefore contain both long-term and short-term gains, taxed separately at their own rates.
Debt-oriented and other fund categories do not automatically receive equity treatment. Classification depends on the fund's asset composition and the applicable rules for the units held.

example.setup: ₹5,000 invested monthly for 18 months, then a full redemption in month 18.
steps: Instalments 1 to 6 have been held more than 12 months, so those units are long-term
Instalments 7 to 18 have been held 12 months or less, so those units are short-term
Long-term portion taxed at 12.5% above the annual ₹1.25 lakh threshold

sections.note: An F&O loss cannot be set off against a capital gain in later years, only against business income. A capital loss cannot be set off against F&O business income. The classification decided at the outset determines what is available later.

Treatment
rows: Taxable at slab rates as income from other sources. TDS applies above the prescribed threshold and is a credit, not the final liability.
Following the change effective from October 2024, proceeds are taxed in the shareholder's hands rather than at company level. Verify the treatment applicable to the specific buyback.
No tax on allotment. Tax arises on sale, including a listing-day sale, which will be short-term.
Interest is taxable at slab rates. Gains on sale are capital gains, with treatment depending on listing and holding period.
Distributions can contain interest, dividend and return-of-capital components, each treated differently. Capital gains arise separately on sale of units.
Gains and dividends are taxable in India for residents. Foreign tax credit may be available under the applicable treaty, with Form 67 and Schedule FA disclosure requirements.
Flat 30% on gains, with only cost of acquisition deductible. 1% TDS under section 194S where applicable. Losses cannot be set off against other income and cannot be carried forward.
